Package hadur2.core.replay

Class LineCodec

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.replay.LineCodec
public final class LineCodec extends Object
Text form of BotInput and BotOrders, one line each, so a battle can be recorded and replayed through the core (CORE-2). Doubles are written with Double.toString(double), which reads back to the same bits, including NaN and infinities. 
 I,time,round,x,y,heading,velocity,energy,gunHeat,gunCoolingRate,gunHeading,
   gunTurnRemaining,radarHeading,others,event;event;...[,numSentries,sentryBorderSize]
 O,bodyTurn,ahead,maxVelocity,gunTurn,radarTurn,firePower[,message;message;...]

An O line carries the tick's messages to teammates (A4) only when there are any, each in Base64, so every line written off a team reads as before.

The sentry fields (M1) are written only when there are sentries, and a scan's sentry flag only when it is set, so lines from battles without sentries, and the fixtures recorded before M1, read the same.

An event is its type letter and fields separated by :. Names escape % , ; : as %XX. Pure string work: no I/O here (RES-6).

Event letters and fields, in the order written:

  • S: scan; name, bearing, distance, energy, heading, velocity, and 1 when the robot is a sentry (GATE-3).
  • H: hit by a bullet; shooter's name, power, bullet x, y, heading.
  • B: our bullet hit; victim's name, power, victim's energy, bullet heading.
  • X: our bullet hit a bullet; our power, x, y, the other bullet's power, our bullet's heading, and from A4 the other bullet's owner when known.
  • M: our bullet missed; power, bullet heading.
  • W: we hit a wall; bearing.
  • R: we hit a robot; name, bearing, its energy, whether it was our fault.
  • D: a robot died; name.
  • K: a skipped turn; the skipped tick (TIME-2).
  • Q: the last core tick's duration and the allowance, in nanoseconds (TIME-1).
  • G: a teammate's message (A4); the sender's name and the bytes in Base64.

Formats only ever grow by appending optional fields, and the decoder treats a missing trailing field as its default (NaN for a bullet heading, not a sentry, no sentries), so every fixture recorded by an older build still replays. Angles are in radians as the adapter reports them, distances in px.
